text:
**redirect**: before landing, fix the no-local-board read so a caller's folder or an explicit `--db` never reads the project's real origin/board-mirror (the same guard the db branch already has, plus `KIT_BOARD_GIT_READ`). Then run `run_all_tests.py --all` again: it is red on cl16 now and green on main.

## Holds
**What holds (rerun on branch cl16 at 76cd5fb, worktree /tmp/review-cl16-the-board-travels-in-git):**
- `check` (`python3 -m unittest tests.test_cl16_board_in_git`): 7 of 7 pass (16.7 s).
- `breaks` (`git checkout 0942fc3 -- .kit/kit.py .kit/board_server.py .kit/board_cli.py`, in a scratch copy): 7 of 7 fail (6 failures, 1 error). So the check can fail.
- Sampled bar, "step change reaches origin/board-mirror: 2 of 2 paths". The server path is test 1 and the kit path is test 4, and both passed. Test 4 runs the kit path in `KIT_MIRROR_SYNC=inline` mode, which no real session uses. So I also ran the real mode: the detached worker, debounced, with `step new` then `step start` inside one window. Origin showed `in progress` after 3.2 s. On the old code it showed nothing after 30 s. Script: `scripts/review/CR-cl16-the-board-travels-in-git-always-current-bg-path.py`.
- `.kit/` and `kit/` copies are the same for all 6 changed scripts (cmp).

**What does not hold: "all suites: 80 of 80 pass".** `run_all_tests.py --all` on cl16: 55 passed, **1 failed** (`tests/test_resume_attached_boards.py`), 24 not run. In a clean environment (`env -i`), the same test passes on main and fails on cl16:
- `test_control_no_attached_board_byte_for_byte`: the new output has an extra line, `9583c05298f1498cacb7 on _orchestrator…`. That is the owner's real 02:58 comment on today's live board.
- Cause, read in `scripts/kit.py`. `open_(m)` → `board_docs(m)`: when `m` has no `board/` folder, it calls `_load_board_docs(m)` with no db_path. With an empty local board, `_load_board_docs` takes its last branch, `_git_copy_docs(m)`. That branch has no "own board only" check, and `KIT_BOARD_GIT_READ=0` doesn't stop it either (I tried). Yet the function's own comment says "never a caller's dir". So resume with `--db X`, or any read pointed at a foreign folder, shows the real board's comments.
- Why the part saw 80 of 80: the test result depends on what is on origin/board-mirror at run time. With no open owner comment there it passes; with one it fails. A test that depends on live board data is the CL48 family ("a test never writes to the real board"), on the read side this time.
- Also on main here: `test_agy_keeps_its_line…` fails only with this container's CLAUDE_*/KIT_* variables set. That one is environmental and not CL16's.

**Not checked:** the 24 suites after the stop. The real project (K2 applies: kit.py, board_server.py, web_takeover.py changed): the post has no `real_project`, so the orchestrator's anlonlt/harmonize run is still pending. The owner's computer runs the old server until `install.py --update` and a restart. The post has no `asked` entry to try as the owner would. A narrow race I read but did not test: the worker can see no pending mark and exit just before a new change's worker fails to take the lock. That change then waits for the next change or the `--final` sync.

## Goal
The train `board-data` serves this: the board is the one record and reads the same from any machine, web session or Artifact, with nothing lost. CL16's bars are sandbox repos, which stand in for that. The owner's own case (posts of 11-22 never reaching git) is reproduced faithfully as test 1: another machine's cursor in sync.json, then a change. That is the right known-good case, and it passes.

The live board still shows the old behaviour, since cl16 is not on main. origin/board-mirror `board/sync.json` still has one shared `db_seq` (1177), going backwards 8 times in the last 447 runs.

What the posts show together: this is the third copy-overwrite loss in the train. 11-22, posts never reached git (CL16). 11-26, an `artifact load` overwrote this very post with an older copy (its `restored_from`). 11-27, CL17's partial pull built 330 writes (CL59, current). Each fix adds a merge path: db+git, git only, Artifact. CL16's red test is one of those paths reading data it should not.

No post shows the owner trying the result himself. The next try after landing is the handoff's own: on his computer, `install.py --update`, restart, and see `[auto-sync] … recovered` or a new post appear on origin.

## Verdict
**redirect.** The fix holds: rerun, it fails on the old code, and the real background path works. But the branch turns a green suite red. The cause is a read path that leaks the real board into a foreign folder, against its own comment. Small fix, back to the same part (cl16 branch). In the last branch of `_load_board_docs`, apply the same rule as the db branch: read the git copy only when `m` is the project's own mirror dir and `KIT_BOARD_GIT_READ` is not 0; otherwise return the worktree files only. Add a test: resume with `--db` on a temp board while origin/board-mirror holds an owner comment, and that comment must not appear. Then `--all` with 0 failed, then this review again.
